members.statement_original: Suppose that $\mathcal P=\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is a finite population of size $N$, and a sample $s$ of size $n$ $(<N)$ is a subset of $\mathcal P$ having size $n$. Further, suppose that $\mathcal S$ is the collection of all subsets of $\mathcal P$ having size $n$. Then, a sampling design $P(s)$ is a probability distribution on $\mathcal S$ such that $0\le P(s)\le1$ for all $s\in\mathcal S$ and $\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}P(s)=1$.

Let $F_{y,N}(t)=\sum_{i=1}^N1_{[Y_i\le t]}/N$ be the finite population distribution function of $y$ for $t\in\mathbb R$. Then, the finite population $p$th quantile of $y$ is defined as $Q_{y,N}(p)=\inf\{t\in\mathbb R:F_{y,N}(t)\ge p\}$ for $0<p<1$.

To eliminate these problems, we consider $\widehat F_y(t)=\sum_{i\in s}d(i,s)1_{[Y_i\le t]}/\sum_{i\in s}d(i,s)$ (see Conti and Marella (2015), Kuk (1988) and Wang and Opsomer (2011)) as an estimator of $F_{y,N}(t)$. Based on $\widehat F_y(t)$, the sample $p$th quantile of $y$ is defined as
\[
\widehat Q_y(p)=\inf\{t\in\mathbb R:\widehat F_y(t)\ge p\}.
\]

members.statement_original: In such cases, a sampling design can be expressed as a function $P(s,\omega)$ defined on $\mathcal S\times\Omega$ so that for each $s\in\mathcal S$, $P(s,\omega)$ is a random variable on $\Omega$, and for each $\omega\in\Omega$, $P(s,\omega)$ is a probability distribution on $\mathcal S$. If a sampling design is independent of $X_1,\ldots,X_N$ (eg., SRSWOR), then, for each $s\in\mathcal S$, the corresponding $P(s,\omega)$ is a degenerate random variable on $\Omega$. Suppose that $\mathcal A$ is the power set of $\mathcal S$. Then, we consider the probability measure $P^*(B\times E)=\int_E\sum_{s\in B}P(s,\omega)dP(\omega)$ (see Boistard et al. (2017a) and Han and Wellner (2021)) defined on the product space $(\mathcal S\times\Omega,\mathcal A\times\mathcal F)$, where $B\in\mathcal A$, $E\in\mathcal F$ and $B\times E$ is a cylinder subset of $\mathcal S\times\Omega$. We denote expectations of random quantities with respect to $P(s,\omega)$, $P$ and $P^*$ by $E$, $E_P$ and $E_{P^*}$, respectively.

Now, suppose that for any $0<\alpha<\beta<1$, $D[\alpha,\beta]$ is the space of all left continuous functions on $[\alpha,\beta]$ having right hand limits at each point, and $\mathcal D$ is the $\sigma$-field on $D[\alpha,\beta]$ generated by the open balls (ball $\sigma$-field) with respect to the sup norm metric. Note that $\mathcal D$ coincides with the Borel $\sigma$-field on $D[\alpha,\beta]$ with respect to the Skorohod metric (cf. Billingsley (2013) and Shorack and Wellner (2009)).

The sampling design $P(s,\omega)$ is called the high entropy sampling design (cf. Berger (1998), Boistard et al. (2017a), Cardot et al. (2014), Conti (2014), etc.) if
\[
D(P\|R)=\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}P(s,\omega)\log(P(s,\omega)/R(s,\omega))\to0\text{ as }\nu\to\infty\text{ a.s. }[P]
\]
(3)
for some rejective sampling design $R(s,\omega)$ (see Hájek (1964)).
Assumption 1. $n/N\to\lambda$ as $\nu\to\infty$, where $0<\lambda<1$.

Suppose that $F_y$ and $F_x$ are superpopulation distribution functions of $y$ and $x$, respectively. Further, suppose that $Q_y(p)=\inf\{t\in\mathbb R:F_y(t)\ge p\}$ and $Q_x(p)=\inf\{t\in\mathbb R:F_x(t)\ge p\}$ are superpopulation $p$th quantiles of $y$ and $x$, respectively, and $\mathbf V_i=\mathbf G_i-\sum_{i=1}^N\mathbf G_i/N$ for $i=1,\ldots,N$, where
\[
\mathbf G_i=(1_{[Y_i\le Q_y(p_1)]},\ldots,1_{[Y_i\le Q_y(p_k)]},1_{[X_i\le Q_x(p_1)]}\ldots,1_{[X_i\le Q_x(p_k)]})
\]
for $p_1,\ldots,p_k\in(0,1)$ and $k\ge1$. Moreover, let $\mathbf T=\sum_{i=1}^N\mathbf V_i(1-\pi_i)/\sum_{i=1}^N\pi_i(1-\pi_i)$, where $\{\pi_i\}_{i=1}^N$ denote inclusion probabilities.

Assumption 2. The inclusion probabilities $\{\pi_i\}_{i=1}^N$ are such that the following hold.
(i) Given any $k\ge1$ and $p_1,\ldots,p_k\in(0,1)$, $(n/N^2)\sum_{i=1}^N(\mathbf V_i-\mathbf T\pi_i)^T(\mathbf V_i-\mathbf T\pi_i)(\pi_i^{-1}-1)\to\mathbf\Gamma$ as $\nu\to\infty$ a.s. $[P]$ for some positive definite (p.d.) matrix $\mathbf\Gamma$.
(ii) There exist constants $K_1,K_2>0$ such that for all $i=1,\ldots,N$ and $\nu\ge1$, $K_1\le N\pi_i/n\le K_2$ a.s. $[P]$.

Suppose that $\operatorname{supp}(F)=(a_1,a_2)$ is the support (see Conti and Marella (2015)) of any distribution function $F$, where $a_1=\sup\{t\in\mathbb R:F(t)=0\}$ and $a_2=\inf\{t\in\mathbb R:F(t)=1\}$. Note that $-\infty\le a_1<a_2\le\infty$.

Assumption 3. Superpopulation distribution functions $F_y$ of $y$ and $F_x$ of $x$ are continuous and are differentiable with positive continuous derivatives $f_y$ and $f_x$ on $\operatorname{supp}(F_y)\subseteq(-\infty,\infty)$ and $\operatorname{supp}(F_x)\subseteq(0,\infty)$, respectively.

In RHC sampling design (see Chaudhuri et al. (2006) and Rao et al. (1962)), $\mathcal P$ is first divided randomly into $n$ disjoint groups of sizes $N_1\cdots,N_n$, respectively, by taking a sample of $N_1$ units from $N$ units with SRSWOR, a sample of $N_2$ units from $N-N_1$ units with SRSWOR and so on. Then, one unit is selected in the sample from each of these groups independently with probability proportional to the size variable $x$.

Let us also assume that $\{N_r\}_{r=1}^n$ are as follows (see Rao et al. (1962)).
\[
N_r=\begin{cases}N/n,&\text{for }r=1,\cdots,n,\text{ when }N/n\text{ is an integer},\\
\lfloor N/n\rfloor,&\text{for }r=1,\cdots,k,\text{ and}\\
\lfloor N/n\rfloor+1,&\text{for }r=k+1,\cdots,n,\text{ when }N/n\text{ is not an integer},\end{cases}
\]
(6)
where $k$ is such that $\sum_{r=1}^nN_r=N$. Here, $\lfloor N/n\rfloor$ is the integer part of $N/n$.
Assumption 4. There exists a constant $K$ such that $\max_{1\le i\le N}X_i/\min_{1\le i\le N}X_i\le K$ a.s. $[P]$.

naming_context.text: Then, one unit is selected in the sample from each of these groups independently with probability proportional to the size variable $x$.

members.statement_original: Assumption 5. The support of the joint distribution of $(Y_i,X_i)$ is not a subset of a straight line in $\mathbb R^2$.

Suppose that the finite population $\mathcal P$ is divided into $H$ strata or subpopulations, where stratum $h$ consists of $M_h$ clusters for $h=1,\ldots,H$. Further, the $j$th cluster in stratum $h$ consists of $N_{hj}$ units for $j=1,\ldots,M_h$. For any given $h=1,\ldots,H$, $j=1,\ldots,M_h$ and $l=1,\ldots,N_{hj}$, we assume that the $l$th unit from cluster $j$ in stratum $h$ is the $i$th unit in the population $\mathcal P$, where $i=\sum_{h'=1}^h\sum_{j'=1}^{M_{h'}}N_{h'j'}-\sum_{j'=j}^{M_h}N_{hj'}+l$. In stratified multistage cluster sampling design with SRSWOR, first a sample $s_h$ of $m_h$ $(<M_h)$ clusters is selected from stratum $h$ under SRSWOR for each $h$. Then, a sample $s_{hj}$ of $r_h$ $(<N_{hj})$ units is selected from $j$th cluster in stratum $h$ if it is selected in the sample of clusters $s_h$ in the first stage for $h=1,\ldots,H$. Thus the resulting sample is $s=\cup_{1\le h\le H,j\in s_h}s_{hj}$. The samplings in two stages are done independently across the strata and the clusters. Under the above sampling design, the inclusion probability of the $i$th population unit is $\pi_i=m_hr_h/M_hN_{hj}$ if it belongs to the $j$th cluster of stratum $h$.

naming_context.text: The condition $\sum_{\nu=1}^\infty\exp(-KM_h)<\infty$ for any $h=1,\ldots,H$ and $K>0$ in Assumption 6 holds, when the number of clusters in each stratum is a strictly increasing function of $\nu$.

members.statement_original: Assumption 7. For any $h=1,\ldots,H$, the support of the joint distribution of $(Y'_{hjl},X'_{hjl})$ is not a subset of a straight line in $\mathbb R^2$, and $E_P\|\mathbf W'_{hjl}\|^2<\infty$, where $\mathbf W'_{hjl}=(X'_{hjl},Y'_{hjl},X'_{hjl}Y'_{hjl},(X'_{hjl})^2)$.

Assumption 8. $\operatorname{supp}(F_{y,h})=C_y$ and $\operatorname{supp}(F_{x,h})=C_x$ for any $h=1,\ldots,H$ and some open intervals $C_y\subseteq(-\infty,\infty)$ and $C_x\subseteq(0,\infty)$. Moreover, $F_{y,h}$ and $F_{x,h}$ are continuous on $\mathbb R$ and are differentiable with positive continuous derivatives $f_{y,h}$ and $f_{x,h}$ on $C_y$ and $C_x$, respectively, for any $h=1,\ldots,H$ and $\nu\ge1$.

Assumption 9. $\sum_{\nu=1}^\infty\exp(-KH)<\infty$ for any $K>0$, and $\max_{1\le h\le H,1\le j\le M_h}nM_hN_{hj}/m_hN=O(1)$, $\sum_{h=1}^HM_h^4/H=O(1)$ and $\max_{1\le h\le H}\sum_{j=1}^{M_h}(N_{hj}-N_h/M_h)^2/M_h\to0$ as $\nu\to\infty$.

naming_context.text: This assumption and Assumption 1 imply that cluster sizes in any stratum cannot be arbitrarily large.

Thus an estimator of $K(p_1,p_2)$ in (8) under stratified multistage cluster sampling design with SRSWOR is obtained as
\[
\widehat K(p_1,p_2)=(n/N^2)\sum_{h=1}^H(N_h^2/n_h-N_h)\sum_{j\in s_h}\sum_{l\in s_{hj}}M_hN_{hj}(\widehat\zeta_{hjl}(p_1)-\widehat{\bar\zeta}_h(p_1))\times(\widehat\zeta_{hjl}(p_2)-\widehat{\bar\zeta}_h(p_2))/m_hr_hN_h.
\]
(16)

naming_context.text: Estimation of asymptotic covariance kernels and confidence intervals

members.statement_original: Given an estimator $\widehat K(p_1,p_2)$ of $K(p_1,p_2)$, an estimator of $\sigma_1^2$ can be constructed as $\widehat\sigma_1^2=\int_\alpha^\beta\int_\alpha^\beta\widehat K(p_1,p_2)J(p_1)J(p_2)dp_1dp_2$, whereas an estimator of $\sigma_2^2$ can be constructed as $\widehat\sigma_2^2=\widehat{\mathbf a}\widehat{\mathbf\Delta}\widehat{\mathbf a}^T$. Here, $\widehat{\mathbf a}=\nabla f(\widehat Q_y(p_1),\ldots,\widehat Q_y(p_k))$, $k\ge1$, $p_1,\ldots,p_k\in[\alpha,\beta]$, and $\widehat{\mathbf\Delta}$ is a $k\times k$ matrix such that $((\widehat{\mathbf\Delta}))_{uv}=\widehat K(p_u,p_v)$ for $1\le u,v\le k$. In the following theorem, we assert that the above estimators of $\sigma_1^2$ and $\sigma_2^2$ are consistent.

naming_context.text: We now discuss the estimation of the asymptotic covariance kernels mentioned in (5), (7) and (8) based on which consistent estimators of $\sigma_i^2$'s will be constructed.

members.statement_original:
Let us assume that $P(s,\omega)$ is one of SRSWOR, RHC and any HE$\pi$PS sampling designs. Let us also assume that $K_1(p_1,p_2)$, $K_2(p_1,p_2)$, $K_3(p_1,p_2)$ and $K_4(p_1,p_2)$ are the asymptotic covariance kernels of the quantile processes constructed based on $\widehat Q_y(p)$, $\widehat Q_{y,RA}(p)$, $\widehat Q_{y,DI}(p)$ and $\widehat Q_{y,REG}(p)$ under $P(s,\omega)$, respectively (see Table 2 and (7)), and $\{\mathbf\Delta_u:1\le u\le4\}$ is a $k\times k$ matrix such that
\[
((\mathbf\Delta_u))_{wv}=K_u(p_w,p_v)\text{ for }1\le w,v\le k\text{ and }1\le u\le4.
\]
(17)

Let us assume that $G(p)$ is one of $\widehat Q_y(p)$, $\widehat Q_{y,RA}(p)$, $\widehat Q_{y,DI}(p)$ and $\widehat Q_{y,REG}(p)$, $K_1^*(p_1,p_2)$, $K_2^*(p_1,p_2)$ and $K_3^*(p_1,p_2)$ denote asymptotic covariance kernels of the quantile process based on $G(p)$ under SRSWOR, RHC and any HE$\pi$PS sampling designs (see Table 2 and (7)), respectively, and $\{\mathbf\Delta_u^*:1\le u\le3\}$ are $k\times k$ matrices such that
\[
((\mathbf\Delta_u^*))_{wv}=K_u^*(p_w,p_v)\text{ for }1\le w,v\le k\text{ and }1\le u\le3.
\]
(20)

members.statement_original: Here, we compare the GREG estimator, say $\widehat{\bar Y}_{GREG}$ (see Cochran (1977), Dey and Chaudhuri (2024b) and references therein), of the finite population mean $\bar Y=\sum_{i=1}^NY_i/N$, the sample mean $\bar y=\sum_{i\in s}Y_i/n$, and the sample median $\widehat Q_y(0.5)$ under SRSWOR in terms of asymptotic variances of $\sqrt n(\widehat{\bar Y}_{GREG}-E_P(Y_i))$, $\sqrt n(\bar y-E_P(Y_i))$ and $\sqrt n(\widehat Q_y(0.5)-Q_y(0.5))$, when the superpopulation median $Q_y(0.5)$ and the superpopulation mean $E_P(Y_i)$ are same.
